cover.tagline: Package once, run the same on any host

items: The `docker` CLI is a client: REST calls over `/var/run/docker.sock`
==dockerd== is the daemon that receives those API calls
==containerd== handles container lifecycle and image management
==runc==, the OCI runtime, creates the actual container process

rows: pid, net, mnt, uts, ipc, user

items: No guest OS to boot: just a ==process== on the host kernel
Start in milliseconds and use **MBs**, not GBs
Image layers are shared, so copies cost almost nothing
**Mistake:** mounting `/var/run/docker.sock` into a container
That container can launch siblings and mount host `/`
Result: ==root-equivalent control== of the whole host

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: Check isolation with `docker top` on the host: container processes show up as ordinary host PIDs.

blocks.title: Interview Point
blocks.text: 1) dockerd vs containerd vs runc? 2) Namespaces vs cgroups: what does each do? 3) Why are containers lighter than VMs?

blocks.title: KEY TAKEAWAYS:
blocks.text: Namespaces hide, cgroups limit, overlay2 layers; one shared kernel makes containers light.

items: ==Image== = immutable, layered, content-addressed template
==Container== = running or stopped instance of an image
A container adds one thin **writable** layer on top
One image can start many containers

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: For reproducible deploys, pin the digest; a tag can be repointed to a different image.

items: `docker ps` lists running containers; add `-a` for exited ones
An exited container keeps its writable layer until `docker rm`
`docker start` revives it with the same files and config

blocks.text: 4. Stop vs Kill vs Exec vs Run

slides.page_title: Running Containers: CMD, ENTRYPOINT and Pitfalls

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: Prefer `docker stop`: it lets the app handle SIGTERM and flush data before the 10s deadline.

items: Using `:latest` in production: not 'newest', changes silently
Expecting data to survive `docker rm`: the writable layer is deleted
Routine `docker kill`: skips graceful SIGTERM shutdown
Pin a tag or digest; mount a volume for data

blocks.title: Interview Point
items: Image vs container?
Stop vs kill?
exec vs run?
CMD vs ENTRYPOINT?

blocks.title: Key Takeaways:
blocks.text: Images are immutable templates; containers are disposable instances, so pin versions and keep data outside.

slides.subtitle: Template vs instance

items: `FROM` sets the base image, starts every Dockerfile; `FROM scratch` is empty
`RUN` executes at build time, adds a ==layer==
`CMD` / `ENTRYPOINT` define runtime behaviour
`WORKDIR` sets and creates the folder; skip `RUN cd`
`EXPOSE` only documents the port; publish with `-p`
==Exec form== `CMD ["node","app.js"]`: app is PID 1, gets SIGTERM directly
==Shell form== wraps it in `/bin/sh -c`

blocks.note: Use exec-form CMD so signals arrive

items: Secrets in `ENV` or `ARG` show in `docker history`
`RUN cd /app` instead of `WORKDIR`
`ADD` for plain files where `COPY` fits
Assuming `EXPOSE` publishes the port

blocks.title: Interview Point
items: ARG vs ENV: build-time or runtime?
COPY vs ADD: which one, and why?
Exec vs shell form: who is PID 1?
Takeaway: FROM first, COPY, exec CMD, no secrets
Each `RUN`, `COPY` and `ADD` creates one cached layer
Change one instruction and the ==cache breaks== from there downward
Order by change rate: base, manifests, install, then source

blocks.note: code edits skip the npm ci layer

items: Chain steps in one `RUN` with `&&`, clean in the same layer
`apt-get update && apt-get install -y x && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*`
A ==.dockerignore== lists `node_modules`, `.git`, `.env`
Smaller build context, fewer cache busts, no leaked files

blocks.note: final image ships only the artifact

items: Builds independent stages in ==parallel==
`RUN --mount=type=cache` keeps package caches between builds
`--mount=type=secret` passes secrets without baking them into layers
Deleting a file in a later layer: **size stays** the same
The earlier layer still holds it; delete inside the same `RUN`
`COPY . .` before the install re-runs it on every edit

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: Run `docker history <image>` to see each layer's size and spot the bloat.

blocks.title: Interview Point
items: How does Docker layer caching work?
How do you shrink an image?
What is a multi-stage build and why use it?
Why is instruction order important?

blocks.title: KEY TAKEAWAYS:
blocks.text: Order layers by change rate, clean up in-layer, ship only the artifact.

items: Container writable layer is **ephemeral**: it dies with the container
Copy-on-write makes writes there ==slower== than a real mount
`docker rm` wipes everything written inside the container
So persist data ==outside== the writable layer
{green:Named volume}: Docker-managed under `/var/lib/docker/volumes`
Create it: `docker volume create data` or `-v data:/var/lib/data`
{blue:Bind mount}: host path mapped in, `-v $(pwd):/app`
Bind mounts suit live-reload dev but tie you to host layout
{orange:tmpfs}: host memory only, never written to disk
`--mount` is explicit and verbose, with key=value options
`-v` is the shorthand, packed into one string
Missing bind path: `--mount` ==errors==
Missing bind path: `-v` silently auto-creates it

blocks.note: throwaway container; tar lands on host

items: Empty host dir bind-mounted over image path ==hides== the image's files
An empty named volume copies the image's files on first use
Running a database with no volume: `docker rm` destroys the data
Anonymous volumes pile up unnamed; name every volume you keep

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: Run `docker volume inspect` to find where a named volume lives on the host.

blocks.title: Interview Point
items: Volume vs bind mount vs tmpfs?
Where does container data live?
How do you back up a volume?

blocks.title: KEY TAKEAWAYS:
blocks.text: Volumes for production data, bind mounts for dev, tmpfs for secrets; never trust the container layer.

items: {blue:bridge}: the single-host default
{blue:host}: shares the host network stack
{blue:none}: loopback only, fully isolated
{blue:overlay}: spans multiple hosts
{blue:macvlan}: gives the container its own MAC on the LAN
Default bridge `docker0` hands out IPs but ==no name resolution==
A user-defined bridge adds ==automatic DNS== by container name
Docker's embedded resolver at `127.0.0.11` answers only there
Same user-defined network: call `http://db:5432` by name
`-p host:container` installs ==iptables NAT== rules
Without it, nothing outside the host can reach the container
`host` driver skips NAT: no isolation, no port mapping, fastest on Linux

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: Run `docker network inspect app-net` to see attached containers and their IPs.

slides.page_title: Service Names on app-net and Network Mistakes

blocks.title: Remember
blocks.text: DNS by name works only on user-defined networks, never on the default bridge.

blocks.note: names resolve only on user-defined networks

items: ==localhost== inside a container is the container itself
Fix: call the service name or `host.docker.internal`
App bound to `127.0.0.1` blocks the published port
Fix: bind `0.0.0.0` inside the container

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: Publish to loopback only with `-p 127.0.0.1:8080:80` so the LAN cannot reach it.

blocks.title: Interview Point
items: Bridge vs host vs overlay?
Why does DNS only work on user-defined networks?
How does -p work under the hood?

blocks.title: KEY TAKEAWAYS:
blocks.text: Use a user-defined network, call services by name, bind 0.0.0.0, publish with -p.

slides.subtitle: Drivers, DNS, port publishing

items: One ==compose.yaml== defines a multi-container app
It declares three things: `services`, `networks`, `volumes`
`docker compose up -d` builds, creates and starts everything
Compose makes a ==default network== for each project
Services reach each other by **service name**, like `db`
Start order: `depends_on` only orders startup

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: Run `docker compose config` to print the merged file with every `${VAR}` filled in.

items: `up --build` rebuilds images before it starts
`-p name` overrides the project name
`down` keeps named volumes unless you add `-v`

blocks.title: Remember
blocks.text: The project name defaults to the folder name; it prefixes every container, network and volume.

items: Assuming `depends_on` waits until the DB accepts connections
Running `docker compose down -v` and wiping database volumes
Forgetting `--profile` so an optional service never starts

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: Run `docker compose up -d --wait` to return only once healthchecks pass.

blocks.title: Interview Point
items: Does depends_on wait for readiness?
How do services discover each other?
Compose vs Swarm vs Kubernetes?

blocks.title: KEY TAKEAWAYS:
blocks.text: One file runs the stack; depends_on orders start, healthchecks gate readiness.

slides.page_title: Registries and the Push and Pull Flow

items: A ==registry== stores and serves images to any host
Public: {icon:docker} Docker Hub, GHCR, GCR/Artifact Registry
Cloud: {icon:ecr} ECR, ACR; self-hosted: `registry:2`
Reference format: `registry/namespace/repo:tag`
A bare name means `docker.io/library/<name>`
Layers are content-addressed by ==sha256==
Shared layers are stored and sent only once
`pull` downloads only the layers you lack

blocks.note: tag must carry the registry host

slides.subtitle: Store, tag, ship images

items: Tag by semver and git SHA for releases
Use `latest` or `1.2` only for convenience
Pin by digest for ==reproducible== deploys
Set retention and lifecycle rules to prune old tags

blocks.note: a manifest list maps arch to image

blocks.text: A ==manifest list== points to one image per platform. The client pulls the entry matching its own CPU.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: Run `docker buildx imagetools inspect iolar/myapp:1.0` to list every platform in a manifest list.

items: Anonymous Docker Hub **rate limits** break CI pulls; authenticate or mirror
Pushing images with embedded **secrets** to a public repo
Deploying a moving `latest` tag and getting surprise changes

blocks.title: Remember
blocks.text: Authenticated pulls get a higher Docker Hub rate limit than anonymous ones.

a_bullets: Digest vs tag: what is the difference?
How do you make deploys reproducible?

blocks.title: KEY TAKEAWAYS:
blocks.text: Tag for humans, pin the digest for deploys, and never push secrets.

items: Containers share the ==host kernel==, unlike a VM's guest OS
A kernel exploit or misconfiguration can **escape** the container
Isolation is weaker than a VM, so layer defences
Run as non-root: root in the container is ==root on the host== without user namespaces
Avoid `--privileged`: it grants all capabilities and host device access
Default seccomp profile blocks about **44** risky syscalls
AppArmor/SELinux add __mandatory access control__ on top

slides.page_title: Image Scanning, Secrets and Security Mistakes

items: Use minimal trusted base images; pin versions, rebuild often
Scan in CI with `docker scout` or ==Trivy==
Secrets: Docker/Swarm/Kubernetes secrets or BuildKit secret mounts
Never put secrets in **ENV**, ARG or COPY; they stay in layers
Verify provenance: Docker Content Trust or `cosign` signatures

blocks.note: Secret mount leaves no image layer

items: Exposing the daemon on tcp ==2375== without TLS
Mounting `/var/run/docker.sock` into a container
Both hand out root control of the host

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: Run `docker run --rm myapp:1.0 id` to confirm the container does not run as uid 0.

blocks.title: Interview Point
blocks.text: Why is running as root dangerous? What does --privileged do? How do you handle secrets and scan images?

blocks.title: KEY TAKEAWAYS:
blocks.text: Least privilege everywhere: non-root, few caps, read-only, scanned images, no secrets in layers.

slides.subtitle: Harden every container

items: `docker logs -f --tail 100 <c>` shows stdout and stderr
The app must log to **stdout**, not to a file
`docker inspect <c>` returns JSON: state, mounts, IP, env, exit code
Extract one field: `--format '{{.State.ExitCode}}'`

blocks.text: Run `docker ps -a` to see stopped containers with their ==exit code== in the STATUS column.

items: `docker stats` shows live CPU, memory and network
`docker top <c>` lists the processes inside
`docker events` streams daemon activity as it happens
`docker exec -it <c> sh` opens a shell to look around
No shell? Use `docker debug` or a **sidecar** sharing `--pid` and `--network`
